title: Heart ultrasound for children (echocardiogram)
what: The doctor uses ultrasound to look at your child's heart: how it is formed and how the valves and walls work. It is safe and painless.
why: For a heart murmur, at the routine 1-month checkup, for shortness of breath, getting tired fast, or changes on an ECG.
duration: usually 15 to 30 minutes; the report is ready right away
tell_doctor: What worries you: a murmur, shortness of breath, blue lips, or tiredness
If heart problems run in the family

prepare.title: Prep
prepare.text: Usually none. Your child can eat and drink.

prepare.title: Calm
prepare.text: Feed your baby before the scan. A full baby lies still more easily.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: Comfortable clothes that are easy to take off on top.

bring: A pacifier, a bottle, or a cartoon, to distract your child
steps: Your child lies on their back, and you stay close
Gel is put on the chest
The doctor moves the probe over the chest, sometimes under the ribs and above the collarbone
Sometimes ECG stickers are put on the chest
The gel is wiped off with a tissue
feel: Babies may cry. The doctor needs your child to lie still, so sometimes there are pauses
after: You can go back to your usual day right away
The report is usually ready right away
Go over the results with your pediatrician or a pediatric cardiologist
red_flags: Blue lips, your child is struggling to breathe, or faints: call emergency services

faq.q: Does a heart murmur mean a heart defect?
faq.a: Most murmurs in children are harmless. The echo shows if there is a problem.

faq.q: Does my child need a sedative?
faq.a: Usually not. Feeding, a toy, or a cartoon helps.

reminders.text: Your child's heart ultrasound is tomorrow. No prep needed. Bring a sheet and something to distract your child.
